overview.headline: Louisiana Purchase doubled nation size and deepened sectional divides

keyPoints.point: The United States purchased vast land west of the Mississippi River and doubled its size westward
keyPoints.quote: signed on April 30, 1803, the United States purchased 828,000 square miles of land west of the Mississippi River

keyPoints.point: Livingston and Monroe were authorized for New Orleans but swiftly agreed to buy entire Louisiana territory
keyPoints.quote: negotiators Robert Livingston and James Monroe were authorized to pay France up to $10 million

keyPoints.point: Jefferson as strict interpreter of Constitution wondered if Government was authorized to acquire territory
keyPoints.quote: was generally a strict interpreter of the Constitution who wondered if the U.S. Government

keyPoints.point: Each expansion greatly increased United States size but exposed sectional weaknesses between North and South
keyPoints.quote: Each expansion, though greatly increasing the size of the United States, also exposed the sectional weaknesses between the North and South

keyTerms.quote: signed on April 30, 1803, the United States purchased 828,000 square miles of land west of the Mississippi River

keyTerms.gloss: President who questioned authority yet approved occupation of new land
